title: Erdos #1084 OQ-01: f_3(n) = 6n - Theta(n^{2/3})
description: Is f_3(n) = 6n - Theta(n^{2/3})? Formalization of the Erdos conjecture on the correction term for unit-distance pairs among separated points in 3D, with proved kissing-number upper bounds and isoperimetric exponent analysis.

meta.assumptions: 4 axiom declarations: degree_le_kissing (degree bound from kissing number), fcc_cluster_pairs (FCC lower bound), bezdek_reid (Bezdek-Reid upper bound), harborth_formula (Harborth 2D upper bound only, not the full equality). Eliminated: kissingNumber (now concrete def with known values), kissing_1d/2d/3d (proved by rfl), degree_sum_eq_twice_pairs (handshaking proved by double-counting). Machine-verified: f1_upper, f1_achieve, 1D triangle/degree lemmas, f2_upper_3n, f3_upper_6n, isoperimetric exponent analysis, erdos_1084_oq01 conjecture decomposition. 0 sorries remain.

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Defines `SepConfig d n` (points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with pairwise distance $\ge 1$), `unitPairs` (edge count of unit-distance graph), and `unitDegree` (number of unit-distance neighbors of a point).

sections.title: One-Dimensional Case: $f_1(n) = n-1$ (Machine-Verified)
sections.summary: Complete machine-verified proof that $f_1(n) = n - 1$: upper bound via left-endpoint injection, achievability via consecutive integers $\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$, triangle lemma ($|x-y|=|x-z|=1 \Rightarrow |y-z|=2$), and degree bound ($\leq 2$ unit neighbors in 1D).
sections.mathContext: Proved: $f_1(n) = n - 1$. Each point has at most 2 unit neighbors (one on each side). The left-endpoint injection maps each unit pair to a distinct non-maximal point.

sections.title: Kissing Number and Degree Bounds
sections.summary: Defines the kissing number $\tau(d)$ concretely with known values $\tau(1)=2$, $\tau(2)=6$, $\tau(3)=12$. Proves the handshaking bound: $\text{unitPairs} \leq \tau(d) \cdot n / 2$. Derives $f_2(n) \leq 3n$ and $f_3(n) \leq 6n$.

sections.title: 3D Lower Bound: FCC Clusters
sections.summary: Axiomatizes the FCC lattice cluster lower bound: there exist 3D separated configurations achieving $\geq 6n - c \cdot n^{2/3}$ unit pairs. Interior FCC points have degree 12; $\Theta(n^{2/3})$ boundary points lose contacts.
sections.mathContext: $\exists c > 0,\, \forall n \geq 2,\, \exists C : f_3(n) \geq 6n - c \cdot n^{2/3}$.

sections.title: The Erdos Conjecture: $f_3(n) = 6n - \Theta(n^{2/3})$
sections.summary: Combines the FCC lower bound with the Bezdek-Reid upper bound ($f_3(n) < 6n - 0.926 n^{2/3}$) to formally state the conjecture. The theorem `erdos_1084_oq01` is proved from these two axioms.
sections.mathContext: $6n - c_1 n^{2/3} \leq f_3(n) < 6n - c_2 n^{2/3}$ for constants $0 < c_2 \leq c_1$.

sections.title: Isoperimetric Exponent Analysis
sections.summary: Defines the isoperimetric exponent $(d-1)/d$ and proves: it equals $1/2$ for $d=2$ and $2/3$ for $d=3$; it is positive and $< 1$ for $d \geq 2$; it is strictly increasing in $d$. This connects the 2D and 3D correction terms to the universal isoperimetric scaling.

sections.title: Connecting 2D Results
sections.summary: Harborth's 2D upper bound $f_2(n) \leq \lfloor 3n - \sqrt{12n-3} \rfloor$ (axiomatized as an inequality; the matching lower bound from Harborth 1974 is not formalized here). Proved: $\sqrt{12n-3} \leq \sqrt{12n} = 2\sqrt{3} \cdot \sqrt{n}$, confirming the $n^{1/2}$ scaling consistent with $\alpha(2) = 1/2$.

overview.historicalContext: This formalization addresses the central open question from Erdos Problem #1084: whether the correction term in f_3(n) is exactly Theta(n^{2/3}). The upper bound f_3(n) < 6n - 0.926*n^{2/3} was proved by Bezdek and Reid (2013) using the isoperimetric method for finite sphere packings. The conjectured matching lower bound f_3(n) >= 6n - c*n^{2/3} would follow from exhibiting FCC lattice clusters with the right contact count. The exponent 2/3 = (d-1)/d for d=3 reflects the surface-to-volume ratio: a ball of volume n in R^3 has surface area Theta(n^{2/3}), and boundary spheres in an FCC cluster lose contacts compared to the 12-contact interior arrangement.
overview.problemStatement: Is f_3(n) = 6n - Theta(n^{2/3})? That is, does the maximum number of unit-distance pairs among n separated points in R^3 have a correction term of order n^{2/3} below the leading term 6n?
overview.text: Formalization of the Erdos conjecture on the correction term for unit-distance pairs among separated points in 3D, with proved kissing-number upper bounds, 1D theory, and isoperimetric exponent analysis.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization builds from the ground up: (1) Complete machine-verified 1D theory (f_1(n) = n-1). (2) Kissing number framework relating degree bounds to pair counts via double-counting. (3) Proved upper bounds f_2(n) <= 3n and f_3(n) <= 6n from kissing numbers tau(2)=6, tau(3)=12. (4) The central conjecture decomposed into FCC lower bound + Bezdek-Reid upper bound. (5) Isoperimetric exponent analysis connecting the 2D and 3D correction terms.
keyInsights: **Kissing number controls leading coefficient**: f_d(n) <= tau(d)*n/2 by double-counting. tau(3) = 12 gives f_3(n) <= 6n
**Isoperimetric exponent (d-1)/d**: The correction term n^{2/3} for d=3 matches the surface-to-volume ratio, just as n^{1/2} in Harborth's 2D formula matches alpha(2) = 1/2
**FCC boundary deficit**: Interior FCC points have 12 contacts, boundary points lose O(1) contacts. With Theta(n^{2/3}) boundary points, deficit is Theta(n^{2/3})
**Bezdek-Reid isoperimetric method**: Proves f_3(n) < 6n - 0.926*n^{2/3} by bounding the surface area of finite sphere packings
**Complete 1D theory**: f_1(n) = n-1 proved constructively with left-endpoint injection and consecutive-integer construction
prerequisites: Euclidean geometry: distance in R^d, inner product spaces
Combinatorial geometry: kissing numbers, sphere packing, FCC lattice
Graph theory: degree bounds, handshaking lemma, double-counting

conclusion.summary: The formalization establishes the framework for the Erdos conjecture f_3(n) = 6n - Theta(n^{2/3}). The complete 1D theory is machine-verified (0 sorry). The 2D and 3D upper bounds f_2(n) <= 3n and f_3(n) <= 6n are proved from kissing number axioms via double-counting. The central conjecture is decomposed into two parts (FCC lower bound + Bezdek-Reid upper bound) and formally proved from these axioms. The isoperimetric exponent analysis reveals the universal pattern: correction term Theta(n^{(d-1)/d}).
conclusion.implications: A proof of the FCC lower bound axiom would resolve the Erdos conjecture for d=3. The isoperimetric exponent framework suggests that for general d, f_d(n) = tau(d)*n/2 - Theta(n^{(d-1)/d}), connecting unit-distance problems to the fine structure of finite sphere packings.
openQuestions: Can the FCC cluster lower bound f_3(n) >= 6n - c*n^{2/3} be proved in Lean?
What are the exact constants c_1, c_2 in the 3D Theta(n^{2/3}) correction?
Does the isoperimetric exponent pattern f_d(n) = tau(d)*n/2 - Theta(n^{(d-1)/d}) hold for all d >= 2?
Can degree_le_kissing (degree bound from kissing number) be proved from Mathlib?

mainTheorems.name: f1_upper
mainTheorems.description: For any 1D separated config on n points, unitPairs <= n-1 (via left-endpoint injection)

mainTheorems.name: f1_achieve
mainTheorems.description: The consecutive integer configuration {0,...,n-1} achieves exactly n-1 unit pairs

mainTheorems.name: pairs_le_kissing_bound
mainTheorems.description: 2 * unitPairs <= tau(d) * n for any separated config (from kissing number + handshaking)

mainTheorems.name: f2_upper_3n
mainTheorems.description: unitPairs <= 3n for any 2D separated config (from tau(2) = 6)

mainTheorems.name: f3_upper_6n
mainTheorems.description: unitPairs <= 6n for any 3D separated config (from tau(3) = 12)

mainTheorems.name: erdos_1084_oq01
mainTheorems.description: f_3(n) = 6n - Theta(n^{2/3}): lower bound from FCC clusters, upper bound from Bezdek-Reid

mainTheorems.name: iso_exponent_monotone
mainTheorems.description: The isoperimetric exponent (d-1)/d is strictly increasing in d

mainTheorems.name: harborth_formula
mainTheorems.description: Upper bound only: unitPairs C <= floor(3n - sqrt(12n-3)) for any 2D separated config of n >= 2 points. Harborth (1974) proved the matching lower bound (the equality f_2(n) = floor(3n - sqrt(12n-3))), but the lower bound is not formalized in this file.
